text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The High Court ruled that a decision to withdraw a 23 percent allowance paid to government security guards and its replacement by a five percent payment is illegal.
- Tswelo, a government-sponsored facility lending to small businesses has withdrawn its lending programme due to a shortage of funds.
- Police officers claim they have not been paid allowances due to them.
- The government has approved an application for a casino to be opened at Lobatse's Cumberland Hotel. Operators are the Sunny Group, which has investments in education and the computer industry.
- Labour and Home Affairs Minister Bahiti Temane has warned Algoa Textiles to adhere to health and safety standards for its workers or face action.
